site.title: Michigan K-12 Data Governance Resources
site.tagline: Order for a Future with Privacy
site.intro: Everything from our Michigan K-12 data governance sessions in one place: the self-assessment, slides, handouts, and the statewide programs that can help your district act on the results. New material is added here after each session.

sections.title: Start here
sections.intro: Five minutes. Twelve questions. Your results by email the moment you submit.

items.title: Michigan K-12 Data Governance Self-Assessment
items.description: Four domains, three questions each, one 1–4 confidence scale. Returns your Confidence Index, three prioritized next steps, and a shareable version with names stripped out.

sections.title: Minimum Viable Governance
sections.intro: Materials and references to help you implement the recommendations from the self-assessment.

items.title: Education Data Governance Framework
items.description: A complete, reusable model for governing education data — built on four domains that together hold up one goal: trust.

items.title: Attachment A - MVG Checklist
items.description: This is a verification instrument, not a to-do list. The Workbook (Attachment B) is where the work happens; this checklist is where you prove it happened.

items.title: Attachment B - MVG Workbook
items.description: Nine worksheets. Fill them in as a team across 90 days; what you produce here is the evidence Attachment A verifies and the artifact set you hand the board at Day 90.

sections.title: Session materials
sections.intro: Slides and handouts from each presentation, posted after each session.

items.title: Securing District Data Through MVG: A 90-Day Cyber Defense & Data Governance Blueprint (slides)
items.description: As K-12 cyber threats and data complexity increase, technology leaders need a practical, integrated approach to safeguard district assets without overburdening IT staff. This session merges cybersecurity defenses with the METL Minimum Viable Governance (MVG) framework into an actionable 90-day blueprint.

items.title: MiGreatDataLake: Data Best Practices & Data Governance (slides)
items.description: Pre-conference session.The MiGreatDataLake (MiGDL) is guided by the P-26 Data Trust—a legal and ethical framework that shifts oversight perspective from managing static data 'ownership' to active data 'stewardship' on behalf of districts.  This session will gather your feedback on your district’s data governance, data use, and data collection practices to best inform the oversight of the statewide educational data trust solution.

sections.title: Michigan programs you can join
sections.intro: Existing statewide programs — you would be joining something, not building it.

items.title: Michigan Student Data Privacy Alliance
items.description: REMC's statewide SDPC alliance: one standard data privacy agreement instead of negotiating vendor by vendor, plus a shared registry of signed agreements.

items.title: MiSecure
items.description: Incident response planning tools, tabletop exercises, the Quick Self-Audit, and the K-12 Operations Center.

items.title: Michigan DataHub
items.description: Interoperability on the Ed-Fi standard, so the same field means the same thing everywhere it lands.

items.title: MiGreatDataLake
items.description: Regional analysis capacity for Michigan ISDs and districts. A Data Trust Board is forming and seeking districts.

sections.title: Laws and frameworks
sections.intro: The citations behind the self-assessment's next steps.

items.title: MCL 380.1136 — Protection of pupil privacy
items.description: Parents may request a list of every third party that received their child's data, and why. Thirty days, no charge.

items.title: MCL 388.1697g — Section 97g, statewide K-12 SOC
items.description: Funds the statewide Security Operations Center and managed detection and response for districts and ISDs.

items.title: General Schedule #2 — Public Schools records retention
items.description: Michigan's approved retention schedule for public school records: how long to keep them and how to dispose of them.

items.title: CIS Critical Security Controls v8.1
items.description: The safeguards each next step maps to, organized by Implementation Group (IG1 → IG2 → IG3).
